findings.title: One-shot ARM rejects a legal in-progress protected-close retry
findings.problem: ARM requires attached host->status_cell. An ordinary timer retry temporarily detaches that exact cell for actual NT close outside remote_lock. The client invokes ARM once and treats any nonzero result as fatal. The prior FAILED_CLOSE snapshot does not reserve the observed !busy/attached state across HostSAFE reads, output, and event creation.
schedule: FAILED_CLOSE samples the protected partial cell reattached with busy=false.
Before ARM, the next ordinary timer retry sets busy, transfers status_cell to its local owner, and unlocks for actual close.
ARM acquires the lock while host->status_cell is NULL and returns ERROR_INVALID_STATE; CHECK21 fails.
The real NtClose fails under protection and ordinary code reattaches the same cell. The server remains correct, but the acceptance setup has failed spuriously.
findings.minimal_fix: Return a transient pending result for the expected busy/detached setup window without committing ARM, and retry ARM under one bounded client deadline until it can latch ready state under remote_lock. Likewise handle BIND existing ERROR_IO_PENDING as bounded setup retry. Do not change ordinary retry ownership or run cleanup from SNAPSHOT.
findings.validation: Qualify setup during an actual in-progress protected close; after reattachment the same real held-control/decision/close checks must run.

findings.title: Armed-but-unstarted worker prevents observation-pin cleanup
findings.problem: Only the entered control hook clears armed, while FINISH rejects any armed state. There is no failure disarm path. Successful ARM followed by CreateThread failure, or elapsed rejection after ARM commits but before worker creation, leaves an auxiliary latch that cannot clear in that invocation.
schedule: ARM commits armed=true and stores the event; no worker is created.
done signals the event, clears the real section protection, and releases the producer. No thread consumes armed.
Actual NT cleanup and Native resource drain can complete.
FINISH still returns ERROR_BUSY because armed remains true. Host/producer observation pins remain retained; done then closes the event/module references without clearing the stale armed event scalar.
findings.minimal_fix: Provide private auxiliary disarm/abort cleanup after the worker is proved absent or joined. Under remote_lock reject a live held/control invocation, then clear unused arm/event state. Follow with existing actual release/drain/FINISH and only then close the event. This must not detach, close, unregister, or repair the ordinary cell.
findings.validation: Cover armed/no-worker and a late ARM response whose side effect was committed. After actual NT drain, observation pins and event must be releasable without process termination.

exact_hooks.result: Only attempted bookkeeping plus an observer after the actual close call returns, outside remote_lock. Actual returned status and remaining cell are recorded; the cell is not rescued/dereferenced by the observer.

The ordinary owns_cell guard remains unchanged. The observer executes after actual reattach/unregister and before busy clear/requeue under the same lock, recording real local owns/attempted/closed/removed and exact cell/owner/registry state.

The event hold runs after real begin_host_status_control admission and lock release, with actual owned control pin still held, before disposal/decrement. Real NT wait and clocks occur outside remote_lock.

Comparison confirms only high identity seed, hook prototypes, appended diagnostic probe/native include. Ordinary packet admission/end implementations are retained. No NT status replacement or ordinary guard weakening is added.

positive_assessments: BIND captures exact own-process producer/root epoch/generation/ticket/context and actual writer HANDLE32 while taking independent host/producer observation references. Those pins do not guard or repair the section owner.

Real failed-close witness requires STATUS_HANDLE_NOT_CLOSABLE and the same remaining cell token after actual close. Client additionally requires attached exact cell, registry/owner counts and !busy. Resource SAFE is not treated as NT-owner completion.

The held decision is selected only with actual status_controls>0, prior actual failure, resource_done, owns_cell=false and attempted=false. CHECK24 requires controls1/busy1 and preservation of the same cell and owner/registry counts. Initialized local closed=0 is explicitly not an actual NT success.

Native fixture state is locked. Worker response fields are read after kernel-thread join. Event lifetime extends through worker exit; the success path joins before close, and failure paths retain event/module when the worker is unjoined.

Protection-clear success is latched before output; no borrowed writer-handle operation occurs after clear, when the timer can close it immediately. SNAPSHOT is observation only. Real post-clear successful close with no partial owner is required; FINISH refuses zero counters alone without recorded actual close success.

Fixed336-byte scalar frame and asserted identity32/count112/decision224 offsets are self-consistent. PE wrapper allows concurrent RUN_CANCEL/SNAPSHOT and reads actual atomic PE counters. Fixture refcount mutations are outside assert; no NDEBUG-only ownership shortcut is introduced.

resolved_findings.status: resolved in v4 and retained in v5
resolved_findings.assessment: ARM now classifies ordinary status_busy as nonacting ERROR_IO_PENDING before testing the attached exact cell token. No event/sequence/arm mutation occurs in that transient branch. When not busy it requires the captured token and commits under remote_lock. Client setup_fixture retries only pending, using one unchanged start time and four-second budget across calls and pacing. BIND uses the same bounded pending handling. An actual successful late commit is not retried: call_fixture records ownership flags before elapsed rejection, then the client enters cleanup.

resolved_findings.status: resolved in v4 and retained in v5
resolved_findings.assessment: DISARM is included consistently as operation6 in header, Native dispatch and PE range checks. It rejects held or started-but-unreturned control work under remote_lock and clears only auxiliary armed/event scalars. Failure cleanup calls it only when no worker exists or the real worker has joined, before event closure and ordinary resource drain/FINISH. Thus an armed-but-unstarted worker no longer strands the observation pins after real cleanup. The normal path exercises unused ARM/DISARM/re-ARM and post-join DISARM without changing ordinary cell ownership.

v5_followup.exact_delta: Only the unused-DISARM check changes from attached cell_present/cell_matches to host_registered, host_owners==1 and actual GetHandleInformation(writer) proving protection still set. No other v5 client bytes differ from v4; all three v5 includes match v4.
v5_followup.assessment: This removes the v4 self-check race with ordinary temporary NT-cell detachment. The protected writer cannot be successfully closed by the intended ordinary retry before the client clears protection, so its real handle remains valid even while the cell is held by the retry invocation. Registered/NT-owner counts remain counted through that work. The following bounded re-ARM still requires the exact cell token under the lock, and the later held-decision check retains the exact-cell assertion. The auxiliary test therefore neither requires a continuously attached cell nor weakens the real ownership witness.

other_assessments: Native DISARM performs no close, detach, registry/counter mutation, ordinary queue operation, control-pin adjustment, signal or wait. Event handle ownership stays with the PE client; no kernel event is closed by Native DISARM.
The existing thread-join requirement protects the raw event borrow, and all changed Native shared fields remain under remote_lock. No new worker/main shared-memory race is introduced by these deltas.
The fixed336-byte frame body and asserted offsets remain unchanged; only the operation enum is extended. Both Native and PE validators accept the same new maximum.

The client has42 normal main-path check calls, including the three new auxiliary checks. Summary and final count predicate both require42. Existing true close/SAFE/held-decision/producer finalization and cleanup checks are retained.

Protection-clear side-effect latches, exact actual failed/successful close observation, read-only snapshots, and the ordinary owns_cell guard/integration are not modified by the reviewed fixture deltas.
